Kodama raises $7 million to expand supervised forestry automation

Equipped machines reportedly moved over 100,000 tons of timber in six months using remote operation and supervised autonomy.

The Robot Report ↗19 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3Videos 1

Funding follows field deployments

Kodama Systems announced $7 million on October 19, bringing total funding to $14 million. Konvoy Ventures and Breakwater Ventures co-led the round. The company plans to expand commercial deployments, develop autonomy and deepen equipment-manufacturer partnerships.

Skidders with remote supervision

The platform currently works on skidders that grip felled trees and drag them to a landing. Automation handles repeatable work while experienced remote operators manage complex situations. Kodama says equipped machines moved more than 100,000 tons across southeastern US states in six months and operate ten to fourteen hours a day.

Building on existing equipment and data

Kodama began with teleoperation and adds autonomy incrementally rather than assuming every worksite can be fully automated. It says it is integrated with two of the three largest equipment manufacturers and wants to extend to cutters and loaders. Its operating figures are company reports, not proof of identical results across all forestry conditions.
